analysis.title: GS - Pasquariello - markets macro - 23 Oct 2026
key_insights: S&P 500 has been range-bound for three months. 60-day realized volatility is about 10%, in the bottom quartile of the COVID and post-COVID era.
The S&P moved only 47 bps this week, while the GS hedge fund VIP pair trade was hit hard again. Pasquariello says the pressure on consensus positions is part positioning, part fundamental.

Hedge fund performance has been in a sustained drawdown since the end of June after a strong first half and a very strong Q2. Investors carried a lot of length in the AI theme, which has now retraced significantly.

GS prime brokerage clients de-risked in net and gross exposure over recent weeks. Thursday saw more tech selling than any other day in the past two years (GS PB). Pasquariello says the market 'cut into some bone' this week but cannot confirm capitulation.

Skepticism toward the AI narrative has risen. Mega caps are executing and demand is not fading, but the market is questioning the supply of POWER and CAPITAL, which creates uncertainty about the path and sequence of the AI buildout.
Oil broke out this week, and the midterm elections are increasingly part of client conversations, with a mostly negative market connotation.

Pasquariello's risk/reward view is unchanged from a few weeks ago: not clear. He has limited conviction and is comfortable 'swimming a bit closer to shore'. He is impressed by the market's resilience on some days and worried about complacency on others.

Pasquariello notes that when he voices this kind of caution, risk/reward has often already improved to favor the bull. Over the past month there has been heavy de-risking among levered investors, implied volatility has firmed, cyclicals versus defensives has been hit hard, and the GS Risk Appetite Indicator turned negative for the first time since March.

Hyperscaler earnings next week are the main catalyst. GS S&P EPS growth estimates (ex-PE) are +29% in 2026, +18% in 2027 and +11% in 2028. If +18% holds, the primary trend stays higher but flattens, so the bull market continues with less punch and more volatility.

Corporate credit price action has been ugly and not limited to AI names. Credit contacts described conditions as 'melting down' more than once. The GS podcast this week covers credit with chief credit strategist Amanda Lynam.
The GS basket of AI leaders has sold off sharply, while the S&P ex-AI is tracking for its best single month in three years. Positioning explains much of the divergence.

sector_views.rationale: Heavy de-risking and retracement in AI leaders, with skepticism about power and capital needs for the buildout, though mega cap demand and execution remain solid.
Cyclicals have been hit hard versus defensives over the past month, which Pasquariello counts as part of the work the market has already done.

earnings_insights: Hyperscaler earnings are expected to drive the market next week.

tension_points.bull_case: Mega caps keep executing, demand is not ebbing, 2027 S&P EPS growth of +18% is strong, bear markets with double-digit earnings growth are rare, and heavy de-risking, firmer implied volatility and a negative Risk Appetite Indicator suggest the market has done a lot of work. The S&P ex-AI is tracking for its best month in three years.
tension_points.bear_case: The market is questioning power and capital for the AI buildout, oil has broken out, sovereign stress and midterm risk are building, credit is weak, and EPS growth decelerates to +11% in 2028, leaving less offset to macro headwinds.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler earnings next week are the next test of the AI spending narrative. A miss on the +18% 2027 EPS growth estimate would undercut the view that the primary trend stays higher.
